terms.label: abbreviation
terms.definition: An abbreviation for a unit is a short ASCII string that is used in place of the full name for the unit in contexts where non-ASCII characters would be problematic, or where using the abbreviation will enhance readability. When a power of abase unit needs to be expressed, such as squares this can be done using abbreviations rather than symbols. For example, sq ft means square foot, and cu ft means cubic foot.

terms.label: alt symbol
terms.definition: An alternative symbol

terms.label: applicable system
terms.definition: This property relates a unit of measure with a unit system that may or may not define the unit, but within which the unit is compatible.

terms.label: applicable unit
terms.definition: See https://github.com/qudt/qudt-public-repo/wiki/Advanced-User-Guide#4-computing-applicable-units-for-a-quantitykind on how `qudt:applicableUnit` is computed from `qudt:hasQuantityKind` and then materialized

terms.label: base dimension enumeration
terms.definition: This property associates a system of quantities with an enumeration that enumerates the base dimensions of the system in canonical order.

terms.label: is base unit of system
terms.definition: This property relates a unit of measure to the system of units in which it is defined as a base unit for the system. The base units of a system are used to define the derived units of the system by expressing the derived units as products of the base units raised to a rational power.

terms.label: byte order
terms.definition: Byte order is an enumeration of two values: 'Big Endian' and 'Little Endian' and is used to denote whether the most signiticant byte is either first or last, respectively.

terms.label: C Language name
terms.definition: Datatype name in the C programming language

terms.label: coherent unit system
terms.definition: A system of units is coherent with respect to a system of quantities and equations if the system of units is chosen in such a way that the equations between numerical values have exactly the same form (including the numerical factors) as the corresponding equations between the quantities. In such a coherent system, no numerical factor other than the number 1 ever occurs in the expressions for the derived units in terms of the base units. For example, the $newton$ and the $joule$. These two are, respectively, the force that causes one kilogram to be accelerated at 1 metre per (1) second per (1) second, and the work done by 1 newton acting over 1 metre. Being coherent refers to this consistent use of 1. In the old c.g.s. system , with its base units the centimetre and the gram, the corresponding coherent units were the dyne and the erg, respectively the force that causes 1 gram to be accelerated at 1 centimetre per (1) second per (1) second, and the work done by 1 dyne acting over 1 centimetre. So $1\,newton = 10^5 dyne$, $1 joule = 10^7 erg$, making each of the four compatible in a decimal sense within its respective other system, but not coherent therein.

terms.label: currency code
terms.definition: Alphabetic Currency Code as defined by ISO 4217. For example, US Dollar has the code 'USD'.

terms.label: currency exponent
terms.definition: The currency exponent indicates the number of decimal places between a major currency unit and its minor currency unit. For example, the US dollar is the major currency unit of the United States, and the US cent is the minor currency unit. Since one cent is 1/100 of a dollar, the US dollar has a currency exponent of 2. However, the Japanese Yen has no minor currency units, so the yen has a currency exponent of 0.

terms.label: currency number
terms.definition: Numeric currency Code as defined by ISO 4217. For example, US Dollar has the number 840.

terms.label: default
terms.definition: The default element in an enumeration

terms.label: defined unit of system
terms.definition: This property relates a unit of measure with the unit system that defines the unit.

terms.label: is coherent derived unit of system
terms.definition: This property relates a unit of measure to the unit system in which the unit is derived from the system's base units with a proportionality constant of one.

terms.label: is non-coherent derived unit of system
terms.definition: This property relates a unit of measure to the unit system in which the unit is derived from the system's base units without proportionality constant of one.

terms.label: is derived unit of system
terms.definition: This property relates a unit of measure to the system of units in which it is defined as a derived unit. That is, the derived unit is defined as a product of the base units for the system raised to some rational power.

terms.label: dimension exponent for amount of substance
element
terms.definition: An element of an enumeration

terms.label: example
terms.definition: The 'qudt:example' property is used to annotate an instance of a class with a reference to a concept that is an example. The type of this property is 'rdf:Property'. This allows both scalar and object ranges.

terms.label: exponent
terms.definition: This property relates a factor unit its exponent

terms.label: expression
terms.definition: An 'expression' is a finite combination of symbols that are well-formed according to rules that apply to units of measure, quantity kinds and their dimensions.

terms.label: factorUnitScalar
terms.definition: For a derived unit that is not exactly the product of its factor units, this property defines the scalar with which that product has to be multiplied with.

terms.label: figure
terms.definition: Provides a link to an image.

terms.label: allowed unit
terms.definition: This property relates a unit system with a unit of measure that is not defined by or part of the system, but is allowed for use within the system. An allowed unit must be convertible to some dimensionally eqiuvalent unit that is defined by the system.

terms.label: base unit
terms.definition: This property relates a system of units to a base unit defined within the system. The base units of a system are used to define the derived units of the system by expressing the derived units as products of the base units raised to a rational power.

terms.label: coherent unit
terms.definition: A coherent unit of measurement for a unit system is a defined unit that may be expressed as a product of powers of the system's base units with the proportionality factor of one.

terms.label: defined unit
terms.definition: This property relates a unit system with a unit of measure that is defined by the system.

terms.label: has quantity kind dimension vector denominator part
derived unit
terms.definition: This property relates a system of units to a unit of measure that is defined within the system in terms of the base units for the system. That is, the derived unit is defined as a product of the base units for the system raised to some rational power.

terms.label: hasFactorUnit
terms.definition: This property relates a derived unit to one of its constituent factor units

terms.label: has quantity kind dimension vector numerator part
has unit
terms.definition: This property relates a factor unit its unit

terms.label: qudt id
terms.definition: The "qudt:id" is an identifier string that uniquely identifies a QUDT concept. The identifier is constructed using a prefix. For example, units are coded using the pattern: "UCCCENNNN", where "CCC" is a numeric code or a category and "NNNN" is a digit string for a member element of that category. For scaled units there may be an addition field that has the format "QNN" where "NN" is a digit string representing an exponent power, and "Q" is a qualifier that indicates with the code "P" that the power is a positive decimal exponent, or the code "N" for a negative decimal exponent, or the code "B" for binary positive exponents.

terms.label: informative reference
terms.definition: Provides a way to reference a source that provided useful but non-normative information.

terms.label: is Delta Quantity
terms.definition: This property is used to identify a Quantity instance that is a measure of a change, or interval, of some property, rather than a measure of its absolute value. This is important for measurements such as temperature differences where the conversion among units would be calculated differently because of offsets.

terms.label: is unit of system
terms.definition: This property relates a unit of measure with a system of units that either a) defines the unit or b) allows the unit to be used within the system.

terms.label: normative reference (ISO)
terms.definition: Provides a way to reference the ISO unit definition.

terms.label: latex symbol
terms.definition: The symbol is a glyph that is used to represent some concept, typically a unit or a quantity, in a compact form. For example, the symbol for an Ohm is $ohm$. This contrasts with 'unit:abbreviation', which gives a short alphanumeric abbreviation for the unit, 'ohm' for Ohm.

terms.label: max exclusive
terms.definition: maxExclusive is the exclusive upper bound of the value space for a datatype with the ordered property. The value of maxExclusive must be in the value space of the base type or be equal to {value} in {base type definition}.

terms.label: max inclusive
terms.definition: maxInclusive is the inclusive upper bound of the value space for a datatype with the ordered property. The value of maxInclusive must be in the value space of the base type.

terms.label: min exclusive
terms.definition: minExclusive is the exclusive lower bound of the value space for a datatype with the ordered property. The value of minExclusive must be in the value space of the base type or be equal to {value} in {base type definition}.

terms.label: min inclusive
terms.definition: minInclusive is the inclusive lower bound of the value space for a datatype with the ordered property. The value of minInclusive must be in the value space of the base type.

terms.label: negative delta limit
terms.definition: A negative change limit between consecutive sample values for a parameter. The Negative Delta may be the encoded value or engineering units value depending on whether or not a Calibrator is defined.

terms.label: normative reference
terms.definition: Provides a way to reference information that is an authorative source providing a standard definition

terms.label: OLE DB name
terms.definition: OLE DB (Object Linking and Embedding, Database, sometimes written as OLEDB or OLE-DB), an API designed by Microsoft, allows accessing data from a variety of sources in a uniform manner. The API provides a set of interfaces implemented using the Component Object Model (COM); it is otherwise unrelated to OLE.

terms.label: description (plain text)
terms.definition: A plain text description is used to provide a description with only simple ASCII characters for cases where LaTeX , HTML or other markup would not be appropriate.

terms.label: Positive delta limit
terms.definition: A positive change limit between consecutive sample values for a parameter. The Positive Delta may be the encoded value or engineering units value depending on whether or not a Calibrator is defined.

terms.label: prefix
terms.definition: Associates a unit with the appropriate prefix, if any.

terms.label: quantity
terms.definition: a property to relate an observable thing with a quantity (qud:Quantity)

terms.label: relative standard uncertainty
terms.definition: The relative standard uncertainty of a measurement is the (absolute) standard uncertainty divided by the magnitude of the exact value.

terms.label: Relevant Unit
terms.definition: This property is used for qudt:Discipline instances to identify the Unit instances that are used within a given discipline.

terms.label: scalingOf
terms.definition: This property relates a unit that is scaled to the base unit that its qudt:conversionMultiplier converts it to

terms.label: standard uncertainty
terms.definition: The standard uncertainty of a quantity is the estimated standard deviation of the mean taken from a series of measurements.

terms.label: standard uncertainty scientific
terms.definition: The standard uncertainty of a quantity is the estimated standard deviation of the mean taken from a series of measurements.

terms.label: symbol
terms.definition: The symbol is a glyph that is used to represent some concept, typically a unit or a quantity, in a compact form. For example, the symbol for an Ohm is $ohm$. This contrasts with 'unit:abbreviation', which gives a short alphanumeric abbreviation for the unit, 'ohm' for Ohm.

terms.label: ucum code
terms.definition:
ucumCode associates a QUDT unit with its UCUM code (case-sensitive).

In SHACL the values are derived from specific ucum properties using 'sh:values'.

terms.label: udunits code
terms.definition: The UDUNITS package supports units of physical quantities. Its C library provides for arithmetic manipulation of units and for conversion of numeric values between compatible units. The package contains an extensive unit database, which is in XML format and user-extendable. The package also contains a command-line utility for investigating units and converting values.

terms.label: unece common code
terms.definition: The UN/CEFACT Recommendation 20 provides three character alphabetic and alphanumeric codes for representing units of measurement for length, area, volume/capacity, mass (weight), time, and other quantities used in international trade. The codes are intended for use in manual and/or automated systems for the exchange of information between participants in international trade.

terms.label: value
terms.definition: A property to relate an observable thing with a value of any kind

terms.label: value scientific
terms.definition: A property to relate an observable thing with a value of any kind
